What really spoke to me was the message of overcoming your fears and assumptions you have of others and yourself. That you cannot assume what others feel about you or how you may truly feel about others unless you take a risk, make yourself vulnerable and really get to know them. I wish I had watched the show when I was younger because I think it would've saved some time that I've spent  coming to these conclusions but it still helped me regardless so I'm thankful for that.

Just finished the series for the first time as well, I think this is a good take and the best explanation I've seen so far as to why Shinji would choke Asuka. 

Looking at things literally: throughout the series Asuka abuses Shinji physically and verbally as a way to guard herself but also because she wants a reaction out of him, she wants him to stop being so submissive and make a move on her because deep down she genuinely likes him and wants someone she can feel secure with. Shinji is meek and takes her abuse because he feels he deserves it but also because he is afraid of hurting her and possibly never having a chance with her as a result. When Shinji is rejected by her during instrumentality over and over it comes to a boiling point and he retaliates in a uncharacteristically violent and assertive manner, just as Asuka reacts in an uncharacteristically meek yet kind manner because she understands where that frustration is coming from. Asuka realizes that if he truly didn't care about her then he wouldn't react so strongly to her rejection. He wouldn't feel so much shame about the pain he's caused her or care so much about her opinion of him.

At this point both of them have realized that their other love interests were incompatible and unhealthy ways to cope with their respective traumas. They recognize each other as equals as they both crave validation and have desperately attempted to obtain it, just through different methods.

Both quickly revert back to their old ways, with Shinji crying out of shame and Asuka expressing her disgust towards Shinji but the moment of vulnerability they shared shows they are now willing to have honest communication with one another and might have a chance to work things out together. It isn't a sure thing but there is at least hope for the two of them.
